grammar.title: Past Simple and Irregular Verbs
grammar.explanation:
We use the **past simple** for finished actions in the past. The time is finished: yesterday, last week, in 2019.

Regular verbs add **-ed**: **worked**, **installed**, **watched**. Irregular verbs have their own past form: **go → went** and **buy → bought**.

In negatives and questions, use **did** + the base verb. We say "I **didn't go**" and "**Did** you **go**?"

The past form is the same for every person. There is no **-s** in the past: "He **worked** late."

**Be** is different. Use **was** and **were**, and do not use **did**: "I **wasn't** tired." "**Were** you at home?"

Spelling: a verb that ends in **-e** adds only **-d**, like **lived**. Consonant + **y** changes to **-ied**, like **studied**. One vowel + one consonant doubles the last letter, like **stopped**.

The economist **worked** in London last year. Use the past simple when the time is finished, not when it is still true now.
examples: *We **went** to the beach on Saturday.* (irregular: go → went)
*She **didn't call** me yesterday.* (negative: didn't + base verb)
*Did you **finish** your homework?* (question: did + base verb)
*My grandfather **worked** in a bank for 30 years.* (finished situation: he doesn't work there now)

practice.q: The economist studies prices every day. → Yesterday, ...
Sara installs new software on the computers. → Last week, ...
practice.a: Sara installed new software on the computers last week.

practice.q: The judge does not listen to the workers. → ...
practice.a: The judge didn't listen to the workers.

practice.q: Do the factory workers go on strike? → Last month, ...
practice.a: Did the factory workers go on strike last month?
